To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ammonia is a strong solvent for hydrocarbon oils at temperatures above 50 °C.
the solubility of ammonia in hydrocarbon oils at high temperature is much higher than expected.
ammonia dissolves in the oil at high temperatures and thus affects the oil viscosity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new lubricants with high thermal and oxidation stability, which are suitable for high-temperature heat pump applications.
the solubility and viscosity of R717 in hydrocarbon oils at high temperatures and pressures, as well as the influence of the oil viscosity and the solubility of the refrigerant.
the development of a method to measure the solubility, the vapour pressure and the viscosity of ammonia in hydrocarbon oils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the solubility of ammonia in hydrocarbon oils increases with temperature, but the viscosity reduction is not as strong as expected.
PAO 6 is the most suitable oil for high temperature R717 applications.
AB oil has the best miscibility with ammonia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the viscosity of the oil–R717 mixtures is significantly affected by temperature and concentration.
it is possible to calculate the viscosity of R717–oil-mixes with high accuracy, but only for temperatures above the miscibility gap.
ammonia dissolves in hydrocarbon oils at high temperatures and thus reduces their viscosity stronger than expected from a simple mixture of two liquids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oil with the lowest viscosity is not always the best oil for a given application.
viscosity charts for R717 compressors should be generated with the oil and ammonia mixture and not with the pure oil.
